# ADR 0003: Check generated artifacts locally

Status: accepted

## Context

"Check" names two different questions, and they need different evidence. Drift asks whether the generated files on disk still match what the metadata declares; answering it means regenerating the outputs and comparing them with the files. Coverage asks whether the model inventory accounts for the project's models; answering it needs the dbt manifest, because only the manifest says which models the project actually has. A single command answering both would need both inputs, would run the expensive regeneration even when only coverage was asked, and could not say which question had failed.

## Decision

Checking is split, and the commands are separate because the questions are separate. `loom generate --check` answers drift: it regenerates every output in memory and fails, naming the files, when a file on disk differs from what the metadata would generate - no manifest is involved. `loom check` answers inventory coverage: it validates the metadata and compares the inventory against the project-owned models in the dbt manifest as one gate, and `loom coverage` reports the same coverage comparison on its own. Neither check writes anything; generation owns writing, and its ownership rule (a generated file carries the `Generated by Loom` header, and regeneration refuses to overwrite a file without it unless `--force` is passed) is what makes the drift comparison meaningful.

## Consequences

A practitioner can gate drift after any metadata edit with `generate --check` alone, and audit coverage after a build with `check` - and a failure always names which question failed. The split also keeps the manifest out of the drift path: a project whose manifest is stale or missing can still prove its generated files are current, and a coverage failure is never reported as drift, or the reverse.
